name: Marcus
oneLiner: 45-year-old home-gym lifter easing back around a cranky right rotator cuff; reports pain persistently.

profile.setting: home gym: dumbbells to 70 lb, adjustable bench, bands, pull-up bar
profile.goals: Rebuild upper-body strength without flaring the right shoulder; stay consistent 3x/week.
profile.injuries: Right rotator cuff strain (6 months old). Overhead pressing and wide-grip pressing hurt; neutral-grip and tucked-elbow work is usually fine.
profile.schedule: Mon/Wed/Fri evenings, 45 minutes hard cap before family time.
profile.personality: Careful, a little wary after getting hurt following an internet program. Reads every note. Loses trust instantly when advice ignores his shoulder.
profile.tolerance: Low pain tolerance by choice — stops sets early. Persistent reporter: mentions the shoulder in almost every check-in.

preferences.primaryGoal: Rebuild strength without aggravating my right shoulder
preferences.limitations: Right rotator cuff strain — overhead pressing and wide-grip pressing hurt. Neutral grip and tucked elbows feel okay.

checkInTemperament.summary: Persistently reports 'too hard' and shoulder pain — prime M4 fodder. Almost never 'too easy'.
painNotes: shoulder ached for an hour after the session
sharp twinge on the last lateral raise set

journey.initialPrompt: Upper body workout I can do at home with dumbbells, a bench, and bands that will not flare up my right shoulder. Nothing overhead, please.
journey.editPrompt: The incline pressing you gave me pinched my right shoulder on the very first set. Take out anything that presses up-and-away from my body — flat or neutral-grip only — and give me more rowing instead.
journey.coachMessage: Be straight with me: is it actually safe to keep training around a rotator cuff strain, or should I just rest it completely for a month? If you would change anything in my saved routine because of this, change it.
journey.followUpMessage: It has been a few weeks now. My shoulder still aches after most sessions and honestly a lot of days feel too hard. Look at how my training has actually gone and tell me what I should do next.
journey.voiceTranscript: Okay so today I did, uh, the flat dumbbell bench with the forty-fives, three sets of ten, shoulder felt okay-ish on the first two sets... then band pull-aparts, I don't know, maybe four sets of fifteen? Then single arm rows with the sixty, three by twelve each side, and I tried, um, lateral raises with the tens but I stopped after one set of eight because the shoulder started talking to me, and I finished with hammer curls, twenty-fives, three sets of twelve.
journey.multiDraftMessage: Build me a push day and a pull day I can alternate — two separate workouts, 45 minutes each, dumbbells only, and nothing overhead for my right shoulder.
journey.painCoachMessage: There it is again — that sharp twinge in my right shoulder near the end of the session. I stopped the set early. Be straight with me: what exactly do we change so this stops happening?
